mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions, which typically precede stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 9.5% in a given month, it signals a tightening labor market that often leads to higher inflation expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 12 months following UNRATE falling below 9.5%, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a policy response to inflation, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising CPIAUCSL and falling FEDFUNDS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% annually), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand for residential construction, which typically precedes higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceed $350 billion, it signals robust consumer spending that typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 12 months following RSAFS exceeding $350 billion, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a supply shock that typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased inflation and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining INDPRO and rising GDPC1 fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply contraction (INDPRO declining below 100.5), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deepening economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO < 100.5, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when UNRATE rises.
